answer_1.quote: We propose a novel and lightweight long-tail inferential knowledge generation framework, Logic-Induced-Knowledge-Search (LINK) ... This framework enables us to obtain long-tail knowledge statements from existing LLMs.
answer_1.outputs: Premise‑conclusion knowledge statements in natural language

answer_2.quote: We calculate the log likelihood over InstructGPT of all statements generated by LINK ... We calculate δ = mean(D(H))/mean(D(L)) for each set of statements ...

answer_3.quote: We use huggingface default implementation of Flan‑T5‑XXL, an instruction‑tuned model that can be used zero‑shot, as the critic that checks data type conformity and factual correctness of the values. We ask the model to output yes/no on the correctness of a given statement.

answer_4.quote: For data type conformity, we ask an AMT worker Is {variable} a {data type}? for each variable in the symbolic rule. For factual correctness, we ask an AMT worker Does the premise entail the conclusion?... We sample 4,000 statements from LINT for human evaluation, of which 2,025 are from head distribution and 1,975 are from long‑tail distribution. We take 3 annotations for each statement and take the majority vote.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators answer yes/no questions about data type conformity and factual correctness of each statement.
